# Penluma — Publishing Playbook (read before adding any blog or topic)

This is the single checklist for adding content to Penluma. Follow it every time so
the recurring manual steps (internal links, cross-links, deploy) never get missed.

**Why this file exists:** most of the site is auto-generated, but a few steps are
manual and easy to forget — inbound internal links, `topics.config.mjs`
registration, and rebuild+deploy. Everything below separates what's automatic from
what you must do by hand.

---

## Definition of done (the short version)

A new post/topic is NOT finished until all of these are true:

- [ ] Content lives in `platform/transformed/<topic>/<slug>.md` (never edit `src/content/blog/` — it's generated).
- [ ] Full SEO frontmatter present (see schema below): `metaTitle`, `description`, `keywords`, `faq`, `author`, `transformed: true`.
- [ ] **Outbound** in-body links: 3–6 contextual links to related existing posts.
- [ ] **Inbound** in-body links: existing related posts updated to link *to* the new post/topic. ← the step that always gets skipped.
- [ ] Post carries `linked: true` in frontmatter once internal linking is done.
- [ ] New topic registered in `topics.config.mjs` (title, description, category, icon, order, `featured` if it's a pillar).
- [ ] A pillar/hub index post exists for a new topic (`00-index-*.md`) linking down to every sub-post — see `PILLAR_STRATEGY.md`.
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds, then `npm run deploy`. Verify live URLs return 200, no broken links.

---

## What is AUTOMATIC — do NOT hand-edit these

All generated from `transformed/` + `topics.config.mjs` on `npm run build`. Adding a
post/topic and rebuilding makes it appear in ALL of these automatically:

- **Topics index** (`/topics`) and **per-topic pages** (`/topics/<slug>`)
- **HTML sitemap** (`/sitemap`) and **XML sitemap** (`@astrojs/sitemap`, built at `astro build`)
- **RSS feed** (`/rss.xml`), **nav / header**, **homepage "Latest"** and topic pills
- **Breadcrumbs, prev/next within a topic, "Continue reading" related posts** (same topic → same category)
- **JSON-LD schema**: BlogPosting, FAQPage (from `faq`), BreadcrumbList — all emitted by `blog/[...slug].astro`
- **OG social images**, **"Related topics" keyword chips** (from `keywords`), **"Further reading"** (from `sources`)
- **`src/content/blog/`, `src/topics.generated.json`, `src/posts.generated.json`, `src/featured.generated.json`** — regenerated by `scripts/import-research.mjs`; edits here are wiped every run.

**Corollary:** if a new topic isn't showing in topics/sitemap/nav on the live site,
it's almost never a missing link — it's that the site wasn't rebuilt + redeployed.
Run `npm run deploy`.

---

## What is MANUAL — you must do these by hand

### 1. Source of truth: `platform/transformed/<topic>/<slug>.md`

- Write/edit content HERE only. `npm run import` overlays `transformed/` onto the raw
  import and **wipes `src/content/blog/` every run** — never edit the generated copy.
- Filenames drive ordering and URLs: `01-slug.md`, `02-slug.md`, … A leading number =
  intra-topic reading order. The hub is `00-index-<topic>.md` (`order: 0`).
- Slug = filename, so the URL is `/blog/<topic>/<slug>` — keep slugs stable once live.

### 2. Frontmatter (full SEO block on every post)

Schema is enforced in `src/content.config.ts`. A finished post looks like:

```yaml
---
title: "Human, curiosity-driven H1 (can be long)"
metaTitle: "≤60-char <title> for SERPs"        # optional; falls back to title
description: >-                                  # ~155 chars, leads with substance
  One or two sentences a searcher sees on Google.
keywords:                                        # target search terms → also renders chips
  - primary head keyword
  - 4-8 realistic long-tail variants
faq:                                             # renders FAQ section + FAQPage schema
  - q: "A real question people search?"
    a: >-
      A direct, honest answer.
author: Brexis Wazik                             # public persona — never a real/internal name
transformed: true                                # marks it as a finished blog rewrite
linked: true                                     # set once internal linking is done
sources: []                                      # optional external "Further reading" (url or {title,url})
topic: <topic-slug>
topicTitle: <Topic Title>
category: <one of the CATEGORIES in topics.config.mjs>
date: 'YYYY-MM-DD'
order: <number>                                  # 0 for hub, else matches filename number
icon: "💸"                                        # matches the topic icon
---
```

Content quality rules live in memory (`blogs-not-research-papers`): catchy title,
strong hook (no "Welcome"), plain conversational language, why-it-matters, examples/
analogies, misconceptions, actionable tips, FAQ, memorable conclusion with a
curiosity hook to a related post. A blog is never a raw research dump.

### 3. Internal linking — BOTH directions (this is what gets missed)

- **Outbound:** every post gets 3–6 contextual in-body links to *related existing*
  posts (same topic first, then genuinely relevant posts in other topics). Use
  descriptive anchor text, not "click here".
- **Inbound:** find existing posts that *should* point at the new one and add links
  there too. A new topic with zero inbound links is invisible to internal PageRank.
  Check with:
  ```bash
  # from platform/ — who links TO the new topic today?
  grep -rl "/blog/<new-topic>/" transformed --include='*.md' | grep -v "/<new-topic>/"
  ```

  If that's empty, you're not done. Add links from the obvious neighbours (e.g. a
  money topic → link from `how-to-make-money`, `personal-money-mastery`,
  `economics-from-first-principles`).
- Mark each post `linked: true` when done. The `workflows/internal-links.mjs`
  workflow discovers un-`linked` posts and inserts contextual links at scale —
  prefer it for bulk work, but it does NOT guarantee inbound links to a brand-new
  topic, so verify inbound coverage manually with the grep above.

### 4. New TOPIC only: register it + build the hub

- Add an entry to `topics.config.mjs` under `TOPICS` (and pick an existing
  `category`, or add one to `CATEGORIES`). Set `featured: true` only for a pillar you
  want on the homepage.
  - Unlisted folders still auto-publish with a prettified title — but you lose the
    curated title/description/icon/order, so always register real topics.
  - Internal/private topics: add with `published: false` (keeps them off the live site).
- Build the pillar hub (`00-index-<topic>.md`, `order: 0`) that links down to every
  sub-post — this is the SEO funnel. Follow `PILLAR_STRATEGY.md`.

### 5. Build, deploy, verify

```bash
cd platform
npm run build          # = import + astro build + pagefind (fails loud on bad frontmatter)
npm run deploy         # = build + wrangler pages deploy → penluma DONT REPLOY AUTOMATICALLY UNITLL HAVE ASKED FOR IT. OTHER WISE ALWAYS ASK
```

- **Dev-server gotcha:** if `astro dev` is already running and you run `npm run import`
  separately, `/blog/...` routes 404 until you restart it
  (`pkill -f "astro dev" && npm run start`). Verify with a curl to a known post URL,
  not just `/`.
- **Verify after deploy:** the topic appears in `/topics` and `/sitemap`, the hub and
  a sample sub-post return 200, and internal links resolve (no 404s).

---

## Quick reference

| Thing                                                             | Where                             | Auto or manual                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Post content                                                      | `transformed/<topic>/<slug>.md` | manual                        |
| Topic title/desc/icon/category/featured                           | `topics.config.mjs`             | manual (per new topic)        |
| Outbound + inbound in-body links                                  | inside the `.md` bodies         | manual                        |
| `src/content/blog/`, `*.generated.json`                       | generated by `import`           | **auto — do not edit** |
| Topics page, sitemaps, RSS, nav, schema, OG, related, breadcrumbs | build output                      | **auto**                |
| Live visibility                                                   | `npm run deploy`                | manual (must run)             |

Related docs: `PILLAR_STRATEGY.md` (hub/funnel template), `README.md`,
`scripts/import-research.mjs` (the generator), `workflows/internal-links.mjs`.
